title: 📘 UNIT 1: DEVELOPMENT OF CAPITALISM AND NATIONALISM 1815–1914
1.1 💰 FEATURES OF CAPITALISM
notes:
Capitalism → an economic system in which most means of production are privately owned and operated mainly for profit.

🏭 Industrial Revolution → strongly accelerated the growth of capitalism.

📍 Origin of Industrial Revolution → England, 18th century.

Industrialized after England → Belgium + France + German states.

⚙️ Major changes → coal and steam replaced wind and water power + factory system replaced domestic production + mass production expanded.

👥 New social classes → bourgeoisie/capitalists and proletariat.

Bourgeoisie → wealthy owners of the means of production.
Proletariat → wage workers who sell their labour.

title: 1.1.1 🏭 Industrial Capitalism and Transatlantic Commerce
notes:
Modern industrial capitalism developed partly from 18th-century transatlantic commerce.

Slave trade and slavery → played an important role in the transatlantic economy.

European wealth came from → colonies + sugar plantations + cotton plantations + tobacco plantations + slave trade.

💰 Plantation and slave-trade wealth → provided capital that helped finance European industrialization.

📍 Liverpool → benefited greatly from slave-trade wealth.
📍 Manchester → textile mills contributed to its growth.

title: 1.1.2 📈 Main Features of Capitalism
notes:
🔹 Private ownership → means of production are mainly privately owned.

🔹 Profit motive → production is undertaken for profit.

🔹 Free market → production and exchange operate through market forces.

🔹 Demand and supply → influence production and prices.

🔹 Competition → producers compete in the market.

🔹 Wage labour → proletariat receive wages for their labour.

🔹 Limited government interference → government imposes fewer restrictions compared with a command economy.

📌 Capitalist economy ≠ command economy.

Capitalism → private ownership + market + competition.
Command economy → government controls production, distribution and prices.

title: 1.1.3 ⚔️ Industrialization, Nationalism and Imperial Rivalry
notes:
Industrialization in Germany and Italy became connected with → militarization + nationalism.

These developments contributed to international rivalry and eventually to World War I.

Germany and Italy → sought colonial empires to compete with established colonial powers such as Britain and France.

title: 1.2 🏳️ NATIONALISM AND FORMATION OF NATION-STATES
notes:
Nationalism → feeling of belonging, loyalty and pride toward one's nation and a desire to support its interests.

Earlier developments that encouraged nationalism →
• Renaissance → development of national languages and literature.
• Protestant Revolution → weakened religious unity of Europe and papal supremacy.
• Expansion of commerce → created wealth and helped strengthen states.
• Trade and colonies → contributed to stronger political states.

📌 Nationalism became a major force behind the formation and unification of nation-states.

title: 1.2.1 ⚖️ Conservatism and the Treaty of Vienna
notes:
After the Napoleonic era → Europe entered a period of political reaction.

Conservatives → wanted to restore the old political order and monarchies.

👑 Treaty of Vienna, 1815 → Britain + Russia + Prussia + Austria worked to reverse changes created by the Napoleonic Wars and restore monarchies.

Revolutionaries → opposed conservatism and promoted ideas such as nationalism.

📌 Main conflict → conservative restoration vs. revolutionary nationalism.

title: 1.2.2 🇮🇹 UNIFICATION OF ITALY — BACKGROUND
notes:
In 1815 → Italy was politically fragmented into several states.

Three major obstacles to Italian unity:

1️⃣ Austrian control → Austria occupied Lombardy and Venice.

2️⃣ Papal States → controlled central Italy and separated northern and southern areas.

3️⃣ Independent states → Kingdom of Sardinia/Piedmont-Sardinia + Kingdom of the Two Sicilies + Tuscany + Parma + Modena.

📌 Many of the smaller states were ruled by relatives of the Austrian Habsburgs and had absolute monarchies.

title: 1.2.3 🧑‍🎓 Giuseppe Mazzini — IDEALIST NATIONALIST
notes:
Giuseppe Mazzini → advocated a united Italy and opposed monarchy.

Carbonari → secret society associated with the struggle against foreign rule in Italy.

1831 → Mazzini founded Young Italy.

🎯 Goal → united Italy under a liberal democratic republic.

1848 → played a leading role in the revolution and briefly led a Roman Republic.

❌ French forces → overthrew the Roman Republic.

title: 1.2.4 🏛️ CAVOUR — POLITICAL ARCHITECT OF UNIFICATION
notes:
Count Camillo di Cavour → became Prime Minister of Sardinia in 1852.

He strengthened Piedmont through → industrial development + railways + agricultural improvement + education + expansion of the army.

Political ideas → opposed absolutism and supported British-style parliamentary government.

🎯 Goal → industrialize and unite Italy.

Austria → identified as the greatest obstacle to Italian unity.

1858 → Cavour secretly agreed with Napoleon III of France to fight Austria.

Cavour promised France → Nice and Savoy in return for French assistance.

title: 1.2.5 ⚔️ CAVOUR AND THE WAR AGAINST AUSTRIA
notes:
Cavour manoeuvred Austria into declaring war on Piedmont.

Sardinia + France → defeated Austria.

Result → Lombardy and Venetia came to Sardinia; France received Nice and Savoy.

Parma + Modena + Tuscany → removed pro-Austrian rulers and voted through plebiscites to join Sardinia.

title: 1.2.6 🔴 GARIBALDI AND THE SOUTH
notes:
Giuseppe Garibaldi → leading nationalist in southern Italy.

🔴 Red Shirts → army led by Garibaldi.

Garibaldi's campaign → captured Sicily → crossed to mainland Italy → conquered southern territories.

He agreed to unite southern Italy with Piedmont-Sardinia and handed power to Victor Emmanuel II.

title: 1.2.7 🇮🇹 COMPLETION OF ITALIAN UNIFICATION
notes:
1861 → Kingdom of Italy established.
👑 Victor Emmanuel II → became king.

At first → Venetia and the Papal States remained outside the new kingdom.

1866 → Italy acquired Venetia after Austria's defeat in the Seven Weeks War.

1870 → French troops withdrew from Italy during the Franco-Prussian War; Italian forces entered Rome.

🏛️ Rome → became capital of Italy.

📌 Result → Italian political unification was completed.

⛪ Pope → continued to govern Vatican City.

title: 1.2.8 🇮🇹 EFFECTS AND PROBLEMS OF ITALIAN UNIFICATION
notes:
⚠️ Problems after unification:
• Regional divisions.
• Limited experience with self-government.
• Industrial North vs agrarian South.
• Conflict between government and Roman Catholic Church.
• Mafia → powerful secret society that the central government struggled to control.

📈 Developments:
• Standard Italian language promoted national unity.
• Industrialization and urbanization expanded, especially in northern Italy.
• Modern education expanded.
• Strong national army was created.

title: 1.2.9 🇩🇪 UNIFICATION OF GERMANY — BACKGROUND
notes:
1815 → Congress of Vienna created the German Confederation.

German Confederation → 39 autonomous states.

Austria → usually dominated the Confederation.

Prussia → gradually became the leading force for German unification.

1848 Revolution → attempted to create a unified Germany but failed.

Obstacles before 1870 →
• Austria, Russia and France.
• Small German states feared Prussian domination.
• Catholic states feared Protestant domination.

title: 1.2.10 🚂 ROOTS OF GERMAN NATIONALISM
notes:
Napoleonic domination (1804–1814) → encouraged Germans to develop a common identity through resistance to French control.

🚂 Railways → made travel faster, easier and cheaper, helping Germans recognize their connections.

1848 Revolution → German liberals promoted unity through:
• Common traditions.
• Education.
• Linguistic unity.

❌ Failure → German ruling classes disagreed about the form of government.

title: 1.2.11 💼 ZOLLVEREIN — ECONOMIC UNITY
notes:
1834 → Zollverein was created.

Zollverein → economic/customs union among German states.

🎯 Main purpose → promote trade and strengthen the German economy.

Main achievement → removed tariffs on goods traded between participating German states.

📌 Economic cooperation helped prepare the way for political unification.

title: 1.2.12 🧔 OTTO VON BISMARCK — THE IRON CHANCELLOR
notes:
Otto von Bismarck → leading force behind German unification.

Background → member of the Prussian Junker class/landed nobility.

1862 → Wilhelm I appointed Bismarck Prime Minister of Prussia.

🎯 Goal → German unification under Prussian leadership.

Prussia's strength → coal in Ruhr + iron and steel industry + strong army + military tradition.

Realpolitik → practical politics; pursuing political goals by necessary means.

⚔️ Blood and Iron → using military power to achieve German unification.

📌 German unification → achieved mainly through Prussian power and top-down royal policies.

title: 1.2.13 ⚔️ BISMARCK'S THREE WARS
notes:
Bismarck used three major wars to unite Germany:

1️⃣ Danish War → 1864 → against Denmark.
2️⃣ Seven Weeks/Austro-Prussian War → 1866 → against Austria.
3️⃣ Franco-Prussian War → 1870–1871 → against France.

🧠 Remember → Denmark → Austria → France.

title: 1.2.14 🇩🇰 DANISH WAR — 1864
notes:
Conflict → began over Schleswig and Holstein.

Result → Schleswig went to Prussia.
Holstein → remained under Austria.

📌 This was the first of Bismarck's three wars for German unification.

title: 1.2.15 🇦🇹 SEVEN WEEKS WAR — 1866
notes:
Main rivals → Prussia vs Austria.

Main issue → leadership of Germany, not merely control of Schleswig-Holstein.

Italy → supported Prussia.

3 July 1866 → Battle of Königgrätz/Sadowa → Prussia defeated Austria.

Results →
• Holstein annexed by Prussia.
• Austria excluded from German affairs.
• Venetia given to Italy.
• North German Confederation formed under Prussian leadership.

📌 Austria's influence over German affairs was effectively ended.

title: 1.2.16 🇫🇷 FRANCO-PRUSSIAN WAR — 1870–1871
notes:
Bismarck → used the edited Ems Telegram to provoke France into declaring war on Prussia.

France → declared war in 1870.

Southern German states → Bavaria + Wurtemberg + Baden + Hesse-Darmstadt joined Prussia against France.

2 September 1870 → French defeated at Sedan.

Result → French Second Empire collapsed.

🏛️ Versailles → German Empire proclaimed there.

1871 Treaty of Frankfurt →
• France ceded Alsace and Lorraine to Germany.
• France paid large war indemnities.

title: 1.2.17 🇩🇪 GERMAN EMPIRE
notes:
1871 → German Empire proclaimed at the Palace of Versailles.

👑 King William of Prussia → became German Emperor/Kaiser.

📌 German unification → completed under Prussian leadership through diplomacy, nationalism and military force.

🧠 Key formula → Prussia + Bismarck + Realpolitik + Blood and Iron + 3 Wars = German Unification.

title: 1.2.18 🇺🇸 AMERICAN CIVIL WAR — 1861–1865
notes:
American Civil War → fought between the Northern Union and Southern Confederates from 1861 to 1865.

Union → opposed slavery and Southern secession.
Confederates → wanted to preserve slavery and establish an independent state.

Most fighting → occurred in the South, causing severe destruction.

📌 Root issue → slavery, connected with deeper economic, social, political and constitutional differences between North and South.

title: 1.2.19 ⚖️ CAUSES OF THE AMERICAN CIVIL WAR
notes:
Major causes →

🔹 Slavery → central disagreement between North and South.
🔹 Economic differences → South depended heavily on cotton plantations; North was more industrial.
🔹 Political differences → disagreement over federal authority and states' rights.
🔹 Social differences → different social structures and attitudes toward slavery.
🔹 Expansion of slavery → conflict over whether slavery should spread into newly incorporated territories.
🔹 Abolitionism → growing anti-slavery movement in the North.

👤 William Lloyd Garrison + Frederick Douglass → important abolitionist leaders.

1860 → Abraham Lincoln won the presidency.

After Lincoln's election → 11 Southern states seceded and formed the Confederacy under Jefferson Davis.

1861 → Civil War began.

title: 1.2.20 👤 ABRAHAM LINCOLN AND THE TURNING POINT
notes:
Abraham Lincoln → Republican president elected in 1860.

Lincoln and Republicans → opposed the expansion of slavery into new territories.

January 1863 → Emancipation Proclamation issued.

📜 Effect → freed enslaved people in areas rebelling against the United States.

Many formerly enslaved people → moved north and joined the Federal army.

📌 Constitutional amendments later strengthened principles of equality.

title: 1.2.21 ⚰️ END AND RESULTS OF THE CIVIL WAR
notes:
1865 → Confederacy was defeated and the Civil War ended.

14 April 1865 → Abraham Lincoln assassinated by John Wilkes Booth, a Confederate sympathizer.

6 December 1865 → Thirteenth Amendment adopted and slavery officially outlawed.

Major results →
• End of slavery in the USA.
• Collapse of the Southern plantation economy.
• Expansion of industrialization in the South.
• Growth of cities, railroads, banks and factories.
• Constitutional changes became a foundation for later struggles for civil and human rights.

title: 1.2.22 🌍 NATIONALISM AND THE 'EASTERN QUESTION'
notes:
Eastern Question → major diplomatic problem of the 19th and early 20th centuries.

It developed because of three major factors:

1️⃣ Rise of nationalism among Balkan peoples.
2️⃣ Decline of the Ottoman/Turkish Empire.
3️⃣ Rival interests of European Great Powers in the Near East.

📌 The Balkans became a major area of international rivalry and conflict.

title: 1.2.23 🗺️ THE BALKANS AND NATIONALISM
notes:
The Balkans → region within the declining Ottoman Empire.

Major peoples → Serbs + Bulgarians + Romanians + Greeks.

Early 1800s → nationalist feelings increased dissatisfaction with Ottoman rule.

By 1830 → Greece became independent.
Serbia → achieved some self-rule.

1850s–1860s → Balkan independence and nationalist movements became stronger.

1875 → revolts broke out in several Balkan areas.

1878 → Romania + Montenegro + Serbia gained independence.

1878–1913 → Ottoman territory in the Balkans continued to shrink, increasing international tension.

title: 1.2.24 🇷🇺 RUSSIA AND THE BALKAN QUESTION
notes:
Russia supported Balkan nationalist movements because:

• Russians were Slavs like Serbs and Bulgarians.
• Many Balkan peoples were Orthodox Christians like Russians.
• Russia wanted access to the Black Sea and Mediterranean Sea.

📌 Russia's support combined cultural/religious connections with strategic interests.

title: 1.2.25 🇬🇧 BRITAIN AND AUSTRIA IN THE BALKANS
notes:
🇬🇧 Britain → wanted to protect its interests in India and prevent Russian expansion toward the Mediterranean.

Therefore → Britain supported the Ottoman Turks against Balkan nationalist movements.

🇦🇹 Austria → supported the Ottoman Empire because it feared Russian expansion in the region.

📌 Great Powers intervened according to their own political and strategic interests.

title: 1.2.26 ⚠️ CONSEQUENCES OF THE EASTERN QUESTION
notes:
The weakening Ottoman Empire created competition among European powers.

Local nationalism + Ottoman decline + Great Power rivalry → repeated Balkan crises.

Between 1878 and 1913 → Britain, Austria, France and Italy acquired/shared former Ottoman territories.

Result → rising tension, hostility and instability in Europe.

📌 The Balkan problem became an international issue because local conflicts were connected with Great Power rivalry.
